text:
Chicago led 2-0 after 11 minutes on two shots that did not look like much. Ryan Donato's wrist shot had an 18 percent chance of going in, and Tyler Bertuzzi's had 6 percent. Buffalo was the team creating the real danger, and the period ended with the Sabres ahead 2.08 to 0.65 in expected goals. Jack Quinn cut the lead to 2-1 late in the first, and the rest of the night was the correction.

Buffalo finished with 64 shot attempts to 38 and 3.93 expected goals to 2.61, which is why the Sabres would win 71 percent of simulated replays of every shot. The middle and final periods were nearly even on chance quality, so Buffalo did not bury Chicago so much as keep pace until its edge counted. Tage Thompson tied it at 2-2 with a tip-in in the second, and Oliver Moore answered with a wrist shot with 1:42 left in the period to put Chicago back in front. Spencer Knight stopped 28 shots but allowed 4 goals on 3.93 expected, so he gave up roughly what the chances warranted.

Rasmus Dahlin tied it at 3-3 with a snap shot 6:10 into the third, and Jiri Kulich scored the winner with another snap shot at 13:20, set up by Owen Power and Thompson. Neither team scored on the power play (Chicago 0 for 2, Buffalo 0 for 3), so all seven goals came at even strength. Kulich, Quinn and Dahlin took the three stars. On the other side, Alex Vlasic had two assists and led Chicago with 22:36 of ice time, and it was not enough to hold a lead the Blackhawks had barely earned.
